title: Keyboard Shortcuts
description: Inside text inputs, Ctrl+C/X/V and Ctrl+Z/Y use the control's own copy, cut, paste, undo and redo. Elsewhere, Ctrl+C copies selected text or the focused word, Ctrl+V does nothing, Ctrl+Z undoes the last staging action, and Ctrl+Y redoes it; on macOS use ⌘, with ⌘+Shift+Z also redoing. Letter shortcuts work when focus is outside text entry. In Words, A, D and U stage an opinion for the focused analysis. In Texts, Enter keeps the focused word's analysis, Shift+Enter keeps it at all the places like this one, Tab moves to the next word without an approved analysis, and Shift+F10 opens the word's opinion tiles. See Passage. In Texts, Up and Down focus the first word on the previous or next line, Page Up and Page Down move by a screen of visible lines, and Home and End focus the first or last line of the Text. For the available display choices, see Settings.
